title: Robert D. Hopper v. James River Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint denied on all five specifications: (1) contrary to the Word of God—denied; (2) contrary to the 1974 Pastoral Letter—denied because the letter did not address a presbytery's power to enjoin such teaching; (3) violation of General Assembly counsel on mutual forbearance—denied, though the Commission urged renewed forbearance; (4) binding the conscience—denied; (5) inconsistency in allowing discussion to presbyters but not congregational teaching—denied. The proposed decision was approved by the SJC 22–0, with 2 disqualified. The April 13, 1991 presbytery action remained in force.
first_summary: The SJC denied TE Robert Hopper's complaint against James River Presbytery's April 13, 1991 order barring him from teaching and preaching his views on prophecy and tongues. The Commission rejected the five specifications and approved the proposed decision 22–0. The presbytery's restriction remained in effect.
summary: The SJC denied Hopper's complaint against James River Presbytery's April 13, 1991 order barring him from teaching or preaching his views on prophecy and tongues. It rejected all five specifications: Scripture did not forbid the order; the 1974 Pastoral Letter did not address presbytery's power to enjoin such teaching; forbearance did not preclude protecting peace and purity; presbytery could restrict preaching short of a heresy finding without binding conscience; and allowing presbyteral discussion while restricting congregational teaching was not inconsistent. The action remained in force.

sources.supports: Case identity, procedural history, complaint specifications, judgment, adopted reasoning, and SJC vote approving the proposed decision.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The source titles the matter '1991-04 — Robert D. Hopper v. James River Presbytery' (line 1). The proposed decision of the Judicial Panel is dated January 31, 1992 (lines 128–133), and the SJC approved the proposed disposition 22–0, with 2 disqualified (line 137).
evidence_notes.dispute: TE Hopper challenged James River Presbytery's April 13, 1991 action reaffirming its confessional position and disallowing him to teach and preach the views of prophecy and tongues found in his 'Final Report' (lines 42–50). His complaint to the SJC challenged that action on five specific grounds (lines 54–58).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC's judgment was that the complaint should be denied (line 62). It rejected each specification: no violation of Scripture (lines 66–78); the 1974 Pastoral Letter did not address presbytery's power to enjoin teaching (lines 80–86); mutual forbearance did not bar presbytery from protecting peace and purity (lines 88–94); presbytery could restrict preaching short of heresy without binding conscience (lines 96–124); and allowing presbyteral discussion while restricting congregational teaching was not inconsistent (line 126).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC expressly declined to make a comprehensive doctrinal statement on the extraordinary gifts (lines 72–78) and declined to decide beyond the complaint whether all JRP statements about the gifts were proper (lines 84–86). It noted JRP had not determined Hopper's teaching was heretical and that presbytery was best able to judge harm to the churches under its care (lines 113–118). It also urged renewed forbearance (line 92).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: The adopted reasoning quotes prior General Assembly materials rather than incorporating a separate decision as the judgment: a 1986 judicial case (M14GA, pp. 125–126) at lines 96–105 and a 1990 18th General Assembly recommendation (M18GA, p. 205) at lines 109–111. The 1974 Pastoral Letter is cited at lines 88–90.

source_limits: The source contains the full proposed decision, the SJC approval vote, and the parties' briefs. The briefs at lines 139–948 are party arguments, not adopted reasons. Lines 950–952 contain an unrelated item concerning SJC Docket 91-5 and are not part of case 1991-04. No separate merits opinion beyond the approved proposed decision appears.
